states.gap: B's advance is wider: line 1 measures 1601px across the same 62 characters against A's 1576px (~26.1 vs ~25.7px per character), so B loses roughly two characters per line at the same 1740px window — line 2 breaks after 'and it was' where A still carries 'and it was not'.
states.gapTheirs: At the same 74px line box and the same dim hex, A sets the type ~6-7% shorter: body ascender 30px vs B's 32px (top y=187 to baseline y=217 vs y=219), x-height 22px vs 23px, dimmed heading ascender 29px vs 31px. At the dim tier's ~1.5:1 contrast (#C1C1C1 on #F7F7F7), the shorter glyph is the one that vanishes first.
states.verdict: These two are the same screen twice over, and pretending otherwise would be dishonest: same #F7F7F7 ground, same #191919 ink, same 74px leading, same 72px text edge, dim tiers one hex step apart. What actually damns both is that the focus state is doing almost nothing here — the second sentence sits at the identical #191919 as the first, so the entire visible effect of 'focus' is a heading faded to about 1.5:1 contrast, which is erasure, not dimming, and there is no caret anywhere in 320px of window to tell the eye where it is meant to rest. B takes it only because when your dim tier is that faint, the 32px ascender survives it and the 30px one doesn't. A writer switching between these would not notice they had moved apps.

states.name: dark-sentence-typewriter
states.gap: Leading is 74 device px per line vs B's 76 (≈37 vs 38 CSS px, ~1.68 vs ~1.75 of the em; body advance measured 26.44 vs 26.05 px/char) — 2px less air per line on a page where 9 of the 11 visible lines sit at #707070 (3.15:1 on #1A1A1A), so the dimmed block clots very slightly more than B's.
states.gapTheirs: B renders a third ink shade: the sentence immediately after the focused one — 'The door took both hands to open.' — is #888888 (4.6:1), sitting between the lit #CCCCCC (10.1:1) and the dim #707070 (3.15:1). 3442 px of it, confined to y896–1076, applied forward only (the preceding paragraph gets full dim). A has exactly two shades in the same region: #CCCCCC and #707070, nothing between.
states.verdict: A dims the way you actually read: one sentence lit, everything else one flat grey, so the eye has a single place to land and no argument about where. B builds a halo — the sentence after your caret is held at #888888, brighter than the rest of the page but not lit, and only forward, never backward, so as you type your peripheral vision keeps snagging on the next sentence you have not written yet. That is the exact failure focus mode exists to prevent, and it costs B far more than the 1px of leading it wins back. B also sets its heading markers flush with the body rag, so '# The Lighthouse' starts 51px right of 'The lamp' while A hangs the mark in the margin and keeps the left edge true.
